PCI.BIO: Dr. Mounir Ben Ghalia is a professor in the department of electrical engineering at the University of Texas Rio Grande Valley. He received his doctorate in electrical engineering from Tennessee Technological University. After obtaining his doctorate degree, he joined the department of electrical and computer engineering at Duke University as a postdoctoral associate and then as an assistant research professor where he conducted funded research on intelligent systems. He joined the legacy institution, the University of Texas – Pan American, in 1999. Dr. Ben Ghalia served as the principal investigator and the director of a National Science Foundation-funded program titled: Research Experiences for Teachers in Emerging and Novel Engineering Technologies (RET-ENET) in the Rio Grande Valley. His funded program supported the professional development of K-12 STEM teachers to introduce engineering education in K-12 classrooms. His research focuses on control systems, robotics, and engineering education; he has published in these areas. He has taught a variety of electrical engineering courses at the undergraduate and graduate levels. He has been selected by the engineering students for several teaching awards and is a recipient of the University of Texas System Regents’ Outstanding Teaching Award.

SCHTEACH.TITLE: Intro to Electrical Engineerin
SCHTEACH.TECHMAT: An important curriculum component of the freshman course is a project that consists in programming the 3pi mobile robot to autonomously navigate a course. Tutorials for programming the robot and a set of mini-challenges were developed. Because most of freshman students taking this course do not have a background in programming, the tutorials and mini-challenges have been useful for providing an experiential learning for students resulting in successfully completing the project navigation challenge.

Each review problem set is tied to a major concept/topic covered in the lecture.  Students are asked to solve the problems on paper and then to verify their answers using the MATLAB software.

CONGRANT.TITLE: RET site: Research Experiences for Teachers in Embedded Systems Engineering
“RET site: Research Experiences for Teachers in Embedded Systems Engineering,
Consortium for Advanced Simulation Testbed for Energy Resiliency Studies
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT: The major goal of the proposed Consortium for Advanced Simulation Testbed for Energy Resilience Studies (CASTERS) is to prepare a sustainable pipeline of highly trained STEM workforce by carrying out transformative research and educating the next-generation of diverse Energy Systems and Smart Grid workforce with strong analytical skills and increased interest in advanced research relevant to the NNSA. In order to accomplish the goal, the proposed CASTERS brings together investigators from two different MSIs of the University of Texas System, i.e., University of Texas Rio Grande Valley (UTRGV) and University of Texas at El Paso (UTEP), with NREL as a national lab partner, and addresses the following four thrusts: 1) evaluation of solar energy resources in South and West Texas, 2) modeling and simulation of renewable energy systems and grid modernization, 3) development of smart grid testbed, and 4) student training, participation and outreach to the community.  The proposed CASTERS also involving six advisory board members, with expertise in power and renewable energy systems, from universities, industry, and national lab will provide a unique platform for under-represented undergraduate and graduate students as well as for faculty towards research growth. CASTERS will involve in various engineering research, but not limited to, solar energy resources including solar irradiance forecasting, smart grid/microgrid and cyber physical system, development of power system studies tools and algorithms, smart building and energy management systems. Thus, CASTERS comprises of interdisciplinary topics that concern many real-world applications such as smart grid, demand response and energy management systems, complex system modeling and optimization, and energy and cyber resilience. In addition, making the existing electric grid to adopt more renewable energy sources has direct impact on national energy security. As part of this proposal we prepare a research monograph that presents the essential concepts, methods, science and technology, and results relevant to global grid optimization. The end product is expected to be a substantial source of knowledge to support graduate and undergraduate students both in terms of research and education at UTRGV and UTEP.
